I am 53 this year. I have farmed these 8 mu for 20 years. My husband works construction in the county town and only comes home on weekends, so the field work is mostly on me. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book.

For the wheat, I planted it last October after rotary tilling. I use Jimai 22, an improved variety — my neighbor Old Wang across the road has planted it for five years and his wheat always looks sturdy. For base fertilizer I put one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, that is 50 kilograms per mu. I bought 8 bags for the whole field. At green-up time in March I already top-dressed with 40 kilograms of urea per mu — I bought 7 bags of urea and had a little left over. Urea is 110 yuan a bag now. Some people in the village say fertilizer prices are too high and we should cut back, but I do not dare. Two years ago I used less urea on 2 mu to save money, and those 2 mu gave me almost 100 kilograms less per mu at harvest. Losing grain is a disaster; wasting a bit of fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate four times total for the wheat: the wintering water I already did, one now at jointing in April, one at heading in May, and one at grain filling. The well pump uses electricity and that costs money too, but without water the grain heads will not fill. I spray pesticide three times — herbicide once, then fungicide when the May humidity comes, and insecticide if aphids show up. I expect about 550 kilograms per mu if the weather does not turn bad.

For the summer maize, after we harvest the wheat in early June I will rotary till again and plant hybrid seed. I need 3 bags of seed, one bag covers about 3 mu, and they cost about 120 yuan each. At planting I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows — I need about 7 bags for the 8 mu. Then at the big trumpet stage I top dress with 40 kilograms of urea per mu, another 7 bags. I irrigate three times for the maize: right after sowing, at jointing, and at grain filling. If the rains are good I might skip one, but last year was dry so I did all three. I spray twice: herbicide before the seedlings break ground, and insecticide for corn borers in July. I hope for 650 kilograms per mu.

Money is tight. My husband’s wages do not always come on time, and with only two of us in the house I have to watch every yuan. The fertilizer and seed for these two crops already cost me several thousand yuan before I even count the electricity for pumping water. But I learned long ago: on these 8 mu, if you try to save money by cutting fertilizer, the land saves you right back with an empty harvest.
